html:
SMTO-CTX-0016 — SMTO couldn't read an attached file as text

GUID: 7c94462e-85c1-4360-ba37-30d2eaf88a3f
Slug: context-read-unsupported-text
Domain: CTX · Subsystem: ctx

What happened

  • A file you attached couldn't be read as plain text. It may not be a text file, it may use an unusual text format, or SMTO started reading in the middle of a letter.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Let the task keep going for a step or two. If SMTO only started in the wrong place, it usually tries again from a valid point.
  2. If it repeats, tell SMTO in the conversation: "Read the attached file again from the beginning." The beginning of the file avoids starting in the middle of a letter.
  3. If the file came from an older program or has non-English letters, open it in a text editor, save a copy as UTF-8 text, and attach it with Add context. SMTO expects UTF-8 text by default, a common format most text editors offer when saving.

What success looks like

  • SMTO's next steps show readable text from the attached file.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the file's name and type, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't rename the file to .txt without converting it; that doesn't change what's inside.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A read_context call could not decode the source or the selected offset as supported text: decoding failed, the text contains a NUL character, or the offset splits a multibyte character (unsupported_text).

What this means

  • UTF-8 decoding failed, the source contains a NUL character or the byte offset splits a multibyte character. Context admission, storage and reading are separate from executing a tool mutation. Preserve existing task state and receipts; a context diagnostic does not authorize replay of earlier operations.

Why this can happen

  • UTF-8 decoding failed, the source contains a NUL character or the byte offset splits a multibyte character.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the source encoding and whether the offset came from next_cursor; starting from a valid cursor distinguishes paging errors from unsupported content.

How to fix it

  • Continue from a returned next_cursor rather than an arbitrary byte offset. If the source is text in another encoding, pass encoding (utf-16-le, utf-16-be, latin-1 or cp1252) to read_context or re-attach it as UTF-8; text containing NUL characters cannot be read by this reader (native/context_reads.py read_source, native/attachment_access.py decode_text). PDF, Office, image and archive files are routed to their format-aware readers instead.
  • Use a supported text extraction and its next_cursor; use a bytes-capable file operation when the source is binary.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The selected text representation decodes cleanly and paging preserves character boundaries.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Context admission, storage and reading are separate from executing a tool mutation. Preserve existing task state and receipts; a context diagnostic does not authorize replay of earlier operations.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
